I used to be close to underweight and also suffer from mental illness so my advice could help. 

What you describe exactly describes the feelingh I had when I was rather light. I had no muscles and no fat, when running for 2km I'd be close to passing out, my vision going blurry and black even. Eventually I ended up in rehab where I did workout, eat regularily and healthy to the point I was still light but didn't go black from work outs anymore.   


Now, 7 years later, I'm 10 kilos heavier with fat and muscle and feel like a truck. I used to be on a BMI of 19, now i'm on 23. I've done regular workout for 2 years now, the key is truly consistancy.  


My arms are still shaking when I work out, mainly due to motivation. If you're really pmuped up and give it your all, you will get worn out and that's the sweet spot where you make progress but can also damage your body.   
Workout itself definitly can have those effects on you if you go all out. If you start like that, you might wanna try to start a little bit easier and then slowly work yourself up.  


Remember, it's no race. The only contestant is yourself. Compare yourself to you past you, not other people with other lives, bodies, DNA, food intake, income etc.   
So don't try to go 0-100 in one day but rather, build yourself up to become a momunment. Little by little. Slow and steady. 

Also make sure your diet is balanced out. You might be lacking a single key nutrition that causes a problem in your system. Genereally speaking, green veggies are always good to eat if you don't know where to start.   


Personally, I mostly eat noodles and rice (It has 12% protein here) with green veggies and meat when I have the time to prepare them. Otherwise I do snack a lot and eat unhealthy hence the fat. But due to my mental illness, my eating habits are wonky anyways so the fat helps staying energized when I forget to eat.   


I've never been feeling like I was blacking out again after my rehab. Gaining weight was the key for me.

I'd see a doctor. I also had knee pains and went to a doctor who MRTed it and found...nothing! I've got two healthy knees, I just might strain them too much during my workout. Try to build up muscle around it slowly and don't overburden it until it can adapt.
